name: French Toast
label: Dischord
lede: Two D.C. lifers who had played in Nation of Ulysses, the Make-Up and Fugazi, friends for twenty years, finally in a band together, and swapping instruments song to song like it was the easiest thing in the world.

eras.title: Twenty years of friendship, first time in a room
eras.text: James Canty and Jerry Busher had been circling each other in D.C. bands since the 1980s without ever sharing a stage. When Fugazi stopped, the drummer who had filled out its live sound and the former Nation of Ulysses drummer finally made a band of their own, and put out their first music on the tiny Arrest Records.

years.h: James Canty and Jerry Busher finally start a band together
years.p: Dischord says [[James Canty|ffc732f4-15a3-42e1-a498-965c1d793e35]] and [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]] had been friends for more than 20 years without ever sharing a band. Canty came out of [[Nation of Ulysses|ae888df0-2a19-4895-a654-e0093875d5b6]] and [[The Make-Up|26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a]]; Busher out of [[Fidelity Jones|c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717]] and eight years touring with [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].
years.xp:
Jerry Busher started with Fugazi as a roadie and ended up playing drums, percussion and trumpet in its live shows, and he is on The Argument (2001). James Canty was Nation of Ulysses' drummer before moving to guitar and organ in the Make-Up.

French Toast was built for two people who could play everything. Both sang, both played keyboards, and Canty and Busher traded guitar, bass and drums depending on what a song needed.

years.h: French Toast's Bug Man EP on Arrest Records
years.p: French Toast's first release, Arrest catalog number are01, three years before the band landed on Dischord.

years.h: French Toast's CD single Hatred Mace / For Sylvia
years.p: A second release on Arrest Records (are03), keeping James Canty and Jerry Busher's duo going while its debut album came together.

eras.title: A duo that sounds like a crowd
eras.text: Four years in, French Toast finally landed on Dischord with a debut album that sounded nothing like the label's reputation: dub, samples, horns and angular funk under sharp D.C. guitars. By the end of the year the two-piece had become a three-piece.

years.p: French Toast's debut: twelve songs co-produced with Bill Skibble and Jessica Ruffins at Key Club Recording Studios. James Canty and Jerry Busher split the vocals and every instrument.
years.xp: It came out on CD and on 180-gram vinyl.

years.p: The Washington Post runs a review of French Toast's debut in its July 1 edition, notice most first albums on a small label don't get.
Dischord says French Toast expanded later in 2005 with multi-instrumentalist Ben Gilligan on bass, guitar and vocals. Now three people rotated instruments on stage instead of two.

eras.title: Not your typical Dischord band
eras.text: The trio took the angular funk on the road and made a second record with Canty's brother at the controls. It turned out to be the last one.

years.h: French Toast opens for [[Supersystem|b900616e-fd32-4c17-8f77-17ae2f1413a0]] at Chicago's Empty Bottle
years.p: Chicago's Oh My Rockness previewed the gig under the headline that French Toast are not your typical Dischord band, pointing to dub, samples and horns instead of punk aggression.
French Toast's first record as a trio, produced by [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]], James Canty's brother and Jerry Busher's old Fugazi bandmate.
years.xp:
Recorded at Blindspot Studios and The Cave; [[T.J. Lipple|ed4cd729-b4d2-4016-a0b6-c362b68d2afb]] mastered it at Silver Sonya.

The credits show how loose the jobs were: Jerry Busher is listed on vocals, guitar, bass, drums, tapes and keys; James Canty on vocals, guitar and organ; Ben Gilligan on vocals, guitar and bass. Twelve songs, including one called Brejnev and a closer called Fork in the Road.

years.p: Dischord lists Ingleside Terrace as the second and final French Toast full-length. The band parted ways in 2006, five years after James Canty and Jerry Busher started it.

eras.title: Everybody's go-to players
eras.text: French Toast ended, but James Canty and Jerry Busher kept doing what they had always done: turning up in other people's bands and making them better. Busher eventually landed behind the kit in Scream, one of the first D.C. hardcore bands.

years.h: James Canty plays guitar in [[Ted Leo and the Pharmacists|31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37]]
years.p: James Canty becomes known as a guitarist in Ted Leo's band, and in 2008 records the digital EP Rapid Response with them as a benefit for Democracy Now! and Food Not Bombs.
The D.C. Afrobeat and funk outfit Funk Ark is one of several bands Jerry Busher plays in after French Toast.

years.h: Jerry Busher takes the drum stool in [[Deathfix|db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123]]
years.p: Busher replaces Devin Ocampo in Deathfix, the band led by [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]], reuniting the two Fugazi alumni.

years.h: James Canty plays keys on Late Night with Seth Meyers
years.p: James Canty becomes the fill-in keyboardist for Late Night with Seth Meyers.
Wikipedia credits Jerry Busher on drums and percussion with Scream, one of the first D.C. hardcore bands, from 2023 into 2024.
